cmd.completion.bash.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(qrypt completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	qrypt completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/qrypt

#### macOS:

	qrypt completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/qrypt

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
cmd.completion.bash.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
cmd.completion.example:
qrypt completion bash
  qrypt completion zsh
cmd.completion.fish.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	qrypt completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	qrypt completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/qrypt.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
cmd.completion.fish.short: Generate the autocompletion script for fish
cmd.completion.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for qrypt for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.
cmd.completion.powershell.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	qrypt completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.
cmd.completion.powershell.short: Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
cmd.completion.short: Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
cmd.completion.zsh.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(qrypt completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	qrypt completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_qrypt"

#### macOS:

	qrypt completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_qrypt

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
cmd.completion.zsh.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
cmd.config.example:
qrypt config init ./qrypt.toml
  qrypt config show
  qrypt config validate --config ./qrypt.toml
cmd.config.export-rclone-password.exampl:
qrypt config export-rclone-password mymount
  qrypt config export-rclone-password --password-file ./password.txt --salt "mysalt"
  qrypt config export-rclone-password --password-stdin --password-hash argon2id --salt "mysalt"
cmd.config.export-rclone-password.long:
Print the password rclone needs to decrypt files encrypted by this config.

If password_hash is "argon2id", the Argon2id-derived key is printed as a hex string.
Otherwise, the raw password is printed unchanged.

Use with a config file (reads encryption settings from the named mount):
  rclone config update myremote password=$(qrypt config export-rclone-password mymount)

Or compute directly from raw inputs (no config file needed):
  qrypt config export-rclone-password --password-file ./password.txt --salt "mysalt"
cmd.config.export-rclone-password.short: Print the rclone-compatible password for a mount
cmd.config.init.example:
qrypt config init
  qrypt config init ./qrypt.toml --force
cmd.config.init.long:
Write a commented starter config (and its local storage directory) to
PATH, or ./qrypt.toml when PATH is omitted.
cmd.config.long:
Create a starter config, inspect the resolved config, validate it, and
export the rclone-compatible encryption password for a mount.
cmd.config.path.example:
qrypt config path
  qrypt config path --json
cmd.config.path.long:
Print which config file would be used: an explicit --config PATH wins,
otherwise the first existing file in the search order
(./qrypt.toml, ~/.qrypt/qrypt.toml, platform config dir).
cmd.config.path.short: Print the resolved config file path
cmd.config.show.example:
qrypt config show
  qrypt config show --config ./qrypt.toml
cmd.config.show.long:
Print the resolved config file with secret values (passwords, salts,
and driver secrets) replaced by ******.
cmd.config.validate.example:
qrypt config validate
  qrypt config validate --config ./qrypt.toml
cmd.config.validate.long:
Check that the config file parses and passes static validation. No remote
drive is contacted, so this is safe to run before mounting.
cmd.config.validate.short: Validate configuration without connecting to remote drives
cmd.control.example:
qrypt control task cancel <task-id>
  qrypt control task retry <task-id>
cmd.control.long:
Control tasks that a running Core owns, such as canceling or retrying a
task, over the local control socket. A Core must be running.
cmd.control.short: Control tasks in a running Core
cmd.control.task.cancel.example:
qrypt control task cancel <task-id>
  qrypt control task cancel <task-id> --config ./qrypt.toml
cmd.control.task.cancel.long: Request cancellation of a task by id. Cancellation is cooperative; observe the task to confirm it stops.
cmd.control.task.example:
qrypt control task cancel <task-id>
  qrypt control task retry <task-id>
cmd.control.task.long:
Cancel or retry a task by id. Cancellation is cooperative; retry starts a
fresh attempt for a failed or canceled task.
cmd.control.task.retry.example:
qrypt control task retry <task-id>
  qrypt control task retry <task-id> --config ./qrypt.toml
cmd.control.task.retry.long: Retry a failed or canceled task by id, starting a fresh attempt under the same task id.
cmd.credential.add.example: qrypt credential add main --type quark --param cookie="k1=v1; k2=v2"
cmd.credential.add.long:
Add a named credential. --type selects the driver and --param supplies
credential-scope parameters such as cookie or refresh_token.
cmd.credential.adopt.example:
qrypt credential adopt docs --name main
  qrypt credential adopt docs --name main --delete-legacy
cmd.credential.adopt.long:
Move a mount's inline credential-scope parameters into a new credential and
point the mount at it. The mount's legacy rotation state is adopted when it
belongs to the same account; the legacy file is kept unless --delete-legacy is
given.
cmd.credential.adopt.short: Convert an inline mount credential into a shared credential
cmd.credential.example:
qrypt credential add main --type quark --param cookie="..."
  qrypt credential list
  qrypt credential show main
cmd.credential.list.long: List credentials with their driver type and the mounts that use them. Secret values are never printed.
cmd.credential.long:
Create and inspect named credentials shared by one or more mounts.

A credential holds the account-scope parameters for a driver (a cookie, a
refresh token, a username and password). Mounts reference it by name and keep
only path-scope parameters such as root_path, so the same account can serve
several directories without copying the secret.
cmd.credential.migrate.example:
qrypt credential migrate docs --credential main
  qrypt credential migrate docs --credential main --delete-legacy
cmd.credential.migrate.long:
Adopt the rotation state a mount accumulated before it referenced a shared
credential. The driver only adopts state that belongs to the credential's
account; otherwise nothing is migrated. The legacy file is kept unless
--delete-legacy is given.
cmd.credential.migrate.short: Move a legacy session into a credential
cmd.credential.remove.long: Remove a credential that no mount references. Move or remove its mounts first.
cmd.credential.set.example:
qrypt credential set main --param cookie="k1=v2"
  qrypt credential set main --remove-param wg_keys
cmd.credential.set.long:
Update a credential's driver type or parameters. --param sets or replaces a
value; --remove-param deletes one. Mounts that reference the credential pick
up the change without editing their own entry.
cmd.credential.show.long: Show a credential's driver type, referencing mounts, and parameters. Secret values are masked.
cmd.credential.test.example:
qrypt credential test main
  qrypt credential test main --param root_path=/
  qrypt credential test s3-main --param bucket=my-bucket
cmd.credential.test.long:
Build the driver from a credential and run its Init once, then drop it.
Mount-scope requirements of the driver (bucket, address, root_path, ...) can
be supplied with --param. The check may refresh and rotate the shared session.
cmd.debug.bundle.example:
qrypt debug bundle --out /tmp/qrypt-debug.zip
  qrypt debug bundle /cloud/photos --out /tmp/qrypt-debug.zip --watch 30s
cmd.debug.bundle.long:
Write a zip bundle of AI-oriented diagnostics: the collect report,
diagnostics, and raw debug endpoints, optionally including a watch report and
path or destination diagnostics for REMOTE.
cmd.debug.bundle.short: Write an AI-oriented debug bundle zip
cmd.debug.collect.example:
qrypt debug collect
  qrypt debug collect /cloud/photos --dest /cloud/backup
cmd.debug.collect.long:
Collect a single AI-oriented diagnostic JSON document: health, state,
uploads, reads, events, cache, staging, and, for a given REMOTE, path and
destination resolution.
cmd.debug.example:
qrypt debug collect /cloud/photos
  qrypt debug bundle --out /tmp/qrypt-debug.zip
  qrypt debug watch /cloud/photos --duration 30s
cmd.debug.long:
Collect read-only diagnostic data from a running Core's debug socket:
health, state, uploads, reads, events, cache, and staging snapshots.
cmd.debug.raw.example:
qrypt debug raw /v1/health
  qrypt debug raw state
cmd.debug.raw.long:
Fetch one debug socket endpoint verbatim. ENDPOINT is a /v1 path such as
/v1/health or /v1/state; the leading /v1/ is added when omitted.
cmd.debug.raw.short: Fetch a raw debug socket endpoint
cmd.debug.read-memory.long: Report recent read-path metrics, such as in-flight and cached reads, with an optional path filter, lookback window, and repeat interval.
cmd.debug.upload-memory.long: Report recent upload part metrics, optionally including upload history, with a lookback window and repeat interval.
cmd.debug.watch.example:
qrypt debug watch /cloud/photos --duration 30s --interval 2s
  qrypt debug watch --duration 1m --jsonl
cmd.debug.watch.long:
Sample debug state repeatedly for a bounded window and report the
transitions and diagnostics observed, optionally scoped to a REMOTE path.
cmd.debug.watch.short: Sample debug state during a reproduction window
cmd.driver.example:
qrypt driver list
  qrypt driver schema quark
cmd.driver.list.example:
qrypt driver list
  qrypt driver list --json
cmd.driver.list.long:
List the names of every storage driver built into this binary, one per
line, or as JSON with --json.
cmd.driver.long:
Inspect the storage drivers built into this binary and the parameters each
one accepts, without reading a config file or contacting a remote.
cmd.driver.schema.example:
qrypt driver schema quark
  qrypt driver schema s3 --json
cmd.driver.schema.long:
Show the parameters a driver accepts, marking required and secret ones,
or emit the same schema as JSON with --json.
cmd.driver.short: List drivers and show parameter schemas
cmd.fs.cat.example:
qrypt fs cat /cloud/docs/report.pdf
  qrypt fs cat /cloud/docs/report.pdf --raw
cmd.fs.cat.long: Write the decrypted contents of REMOTE to stdout; use --raw for the backend bytes without decryption or read-cache transforms.
cmd.fs.cat.short: Write a remote file to stdout
cmd.fs.check.example:
qrypt fs check /cloud/photos ./photos
  qrypt fs check /cloud/photos ./photos --compare hash
cmd.fs.check.long:
Check that the trees at A and B contain the same files.

A and B can be virtual paths under a configured mount (/MOUNT/dir) or local
paths. Encryption is handled transparently: the mount's [mounts.encryption]
is applied when comparing, so a local plaintext directory can be checked
against an encrypted cloud mount.

Differences are reported relative to the argument order: missing_in_b means
a file exists on A but not B; extra_in_b means it exists on B but not A.

Exit code: 0 when identical, 4 when differences are found, 1 on errors.
cmd.fs.check.short: Check that two trees contain the same files
cmd.fs.copy.long: Copy SOURCE to DESTINATION directly between mounted backends, without downloading through the local machine. Use --recursive for directories.
cmd.fs.copy.short: Copy a remote file directly between mounted backends
cmd.fs.crypt-decode.example:
qrypt fs crypt-decode cloud /cloud/photos/8f3a2b...
  qrypt fs crypt-decode 8f3a2b...
cmd.fs.crypt-decode.long:
Decrypt NAME (ciphertext name as stored on the backend) back to the
plaintext virtual path, using the mount's [mounts.encryption] settings.
Useful to identify which local file a backend filename belongs to.

MOUNT defaults to the first mount with encryption configured.
cmd.fs.crypt-decode.short: Decrypt an encrypted filename to its plaintext
cmd.fs.crypt-encode.example:
qrypt fs crypt-encode /cloud/photos/cat.jpg
  qrypt fs crypt-encode cloud /cloud/photos/cat.jpg
cmd.fs.crypt-encode.long:
Encrypt NAME (plaintext virtual path) into the ciphertext filename
stored on the backend, using the mount's [mounts.encryption] settings.
Useful to verify what a plaintext name looks like on the remote drive.

MOUNT defaults to the first mount with encryption configured.
cmd.fs.crypt-encode.short: Encrypt a filename with a mount's encryption config
cmd.fs.df.example:
qrypt fs df
  qrypt fs df cloud --bytes
cmd.fs.df.long: Show total, free, and used space for the configured drives, or for one MOUNT when given.
cmd.fs.df.short: Show space usage of the configured drives
cmd.fs.du.example:
qrypt fs du /cloud/photos
  qrypt fs du /cloud/photos --bytes
cmd.fs.du.long: Show the file count and total bytes of the tree at REMOTE, or of the namespace root when REMOTE is omitted.
cmd.fs.du.short: Show disk usage of a directory tree
cmd.fs.example:
qrypt fs list /cloud/photos
  qrypt fs get /cloud/photos/cat.jpg ./cat.jpg
  qrypt fs put ./report.pdf /cloud/docs/report.pdf
cmd.fs.find.example:
qrypt fs find photo /cloud
  qrypt fs find --json ".jpg" /cloud/photos
cmd.fs.find.long: Recursively search REMOTE (default /) for entries whose name contains NAME, case-insensitively, and print each match's full path.
cmd.fs.find.short: Recursively find entries whose name contains NAME
cmd.fs.get.example:
qrypt fs get /cloud/photos/cat.jpg ./cat.jpg
  qrypt fs get /cloud/photos ./photos --force
cmd.fs.get.long:
Download REMOTE to the local path LOCAL. A directory is downloaded
recursively under LOCAL; an existing local file is skipped unless --force.
cmd.fs.get.short: Download a remote file or directory
cmd.fs.journal.example:
qrypt fs journal
  qrypt fs journal replay --mount cloud
  qrypt fs journal prune --mount cloud
cmd.fs.journal.long:
Inspect the offline upload journal and repair it: replay failed uploads
so the next mount retries them, or prune entries whose staging data is gone.
cmd.fs.journal.prune.example:
qrypt fs journal prune
  qrypt fs journal prune --mount cloud
cmd.fs.journal.prune.long: Drop journal entries for offline uploads whose local staging data no longer exists.
cmd.fs.journal.prune.short: Drop offline uploads whose staging data is gone
cmd.fs.journal.replay.example:
qrypt fs journal replay
  qrypt fs journal replay --mount cloud
cmd.fs.journal.replay.long: Reset failed offline uploads in the journal so the next mount retries them.
cmd.fs.journal.replay.short: Reset failed offline uploads so the next mount retries them
cmd.fs.journal.short: Inspect and maintain the offline upload journal
cmd.fs.list.example:
qrypt fs list /cloud/photos
  qrypt fs list /cloud/photos --human
cmd.fs.list.long: List the entries of REMOTE, or the namespace root when REMOTE is omitted.
cmd.fs.long:
Run one-shot filesystem operations against the configured mounts: list,
read, write, transfer, compare, and inspect files without mounting.
cmd.fs.mv.long: Rename or move SOURCE to DESTINATION.
cmd.fs.pending.example:
qrypt fs pending
  qrypt fs pending --verbose
cmd.fs.pending.long:
Show the files waiting to be uploaded from the local staging area, with
their sizes and local paths; --verbose adds retry and staging status.
cmd.fs.put.example:
qrypt fs put ./report.pdf /cloud/docs/report.pdf
  cat report.pdf | qrypt fs put - /cloud/docs/report.pdf
cmd.fs.put.long:
Upload the local file LOCAL to REMOTE. Pass - as LOCAL to read the
contents from standard input.
cmd.fs.put.short: Upload a local file; use - to read from stdin
cmd.fs.rm.long: Remove the file or empty directory REMOTE, waiting for the deletion to reach the backend.
cmd.fs.rm.short: Remove a file or empty directory
cmd.fs.stat.long: Show the size, type, and modification time of REMOTE.
cmd.fs.sync.example:
qrypt fs sync ./photos /cloud/photos
  qrypt fs sync /cloud/photos ./photos --delete --dry-run
cmd.fs.sync.long:
Synchronize the tree at DESTINATION to match the tree at SOURCE.

SOURCE is authoritative; DESTINATION is modified. Files missing on
DESTINATION are added, changed files are updated, and extra files on
DESTINATION are left alone unless --delete is given. Type conflicts
(file vs directory on the same path) are reported and skipped by
default; use --conflict=source to let SOURCE win.

At least one side must be a virtual path (/MOUNT/dir). Local paths are
compared against the VFS plaintext view (encryption is transparent).

Exit code: 0 on success (also for --dry-run plans), 3 when some files
failed, 2 on usage errors, 1 on overall failures.
cmd.fs.sync.short: Make DESTINATION match SOURCE (one-way, non-destructive by default)
cmd.help.long:
Help provides help for any command in the application.
Simply type qrypt help [path to command] for full details.
cmd.mount.add.example:
qrypt mount add docs --credential main --param root_path=/Docs
  qrypt mount add photos --credential main --param root_path=/Photos --password "secret"
  qrypt mount add vault --credential main --param root_path=/Vault --password "secret" --filename-encryption obfuscate
cmd.mount.add.long:
Add a mount that uses a credential declared in [[credentials]]. The driver
type comes from the credential, so only mount-scope attributes (root_path and
other path-scope params, test_enabled, optional encryption) are configured
here. Encryption flags mirror [mounts.encryption]: --password enables it, and
--salt / --filename-encryption / --filename-encoding / --content-dedup tune it.
Mount names add, set, remove, and list are reserved for subcommands.
cmd.mount.add.short: Add a mount from an existing credential
cmd.mount.list.long: List mounts with their driver type, referenced credential, and configured root_path.
cmd.mount.long: Mount all configured drives as one local FUSE filesystem, or mount one configured drive by name. Uses mount_point from config unless --mount-point is set.
cmd.mount.remove.long: Remove a mount from the configuration. The referenced credential is kept; remove it separately with qrypt credential remove.
cmd.mount.set.example:
qrypt mount set docs --param root_path=/Documents
  qrypt mount set docs --credential other-main
  qrypt mount set docs --password "new-secret" --force
cmd.mount.set.long:
Update an existing mount. --credential switches it to another declared
credential (the driver type follows the new credential); --param sets or
replaces a mount-scope parameter and --remove-param deletes one.

Encryption flags mirror [mounts.encryption]. Adding encryption to an
unencrypted mount needs only --password. Encryption cannot be removed once
configured; changing its password, salt, or filename mode requires --force,
because existing remote data may become unreadable.
cmd.mount.set.short: Update a mount's credential or attributes
cmd.offline.add.example:
qrypt offline add "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:..." --parse-to /quark/downloads
  qrypt offline add ./movie.torrent --mount quark --mkdir
  qrypt offline add https://example.com/file.iso --parse-to /quark/downloads --select largest:1 --wait
cmd.offline.add.long:
Submit a magnet link, HTTP(S)/FTP URL, or local .torrent file to the
provider's offline download service. The parse destination mount selects the
provider; the cloud-side result stays on the provider.
cmd.offline.add.short: Submit a source as a cloud-side offline download
cmd.offline.cancel.long: Request cancellation of an offline task. Cancellation is cooperative; observe the task to confirm it reaches the canceled state.
cmd.offline.example:
qrypt offline add "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:..." --parse-to /quark/downloads
  qrypt offline fetch https://example.com/file.iso --mount quark --download-to ~/Downloads
  qrypt offline inspect ./movie.torrent --mount quark
  qrypt offline list --all
cmd.offline.fetch.example:
qrypt offline fetch "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:..." --parse-to /quark/downloads --download-to ~/Downloads
  qrypt offline fetch https://example.com/file.iso --parse-to /quark/downloads --download-to ./out/ --keep-cloud
  qrypt offline fetch "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:..." --mount quark --download-to ~/Downloads --wait
cmd.offline.fetch.long:
Stage a source on the provider, then transfer the result to --download-to.
The destination may be a qrypt namespace path, a path inside the mount tree, or
a plain local path. When it is a directory, each selected file is written under
it at its staged relative path, recreating the provider's folders; --flat writes
by file name instead. By default the command prints the task and returns while
the transfer continues in the Core; --wait blocks until the destination is
written and renders progress.
cmd.offline.fetch.short: Stage a source in the cloud, then transfer it to a final destination
cmd.offline.inspect.example:
qrypt offline inspect "magnet:?xt=urn:btih:..." --parse-to /quark/downloads
  qrypt offline inspect ./movie.torrent --mount quark --select largest:3
cmd.offline.inspect.long:
Parse a source and report its files, total size, instant-save prediction,
and parse-destination checks without creating a task.
cmd.offline.inspect.short: Preview a source without creating a task
cmd.offline.list.example:
qrypt offline list
  qrypt offline list --all --state failed --limit 50
cmd.offline.list.long:
List offline tasks. Active and failed tasks are shown by default; use
--all to include succeeded and canceled ones, and --state or --mount to
narrow the result.
cmd.offline.list.short: List offline tasks (active and failed by default)
cmd.offline.long:
Submit a source to a cloud drive's offline download service and control
the resulting provider task. Provider selection is the parse destination mount;
no provider name or task id is ever required.

  qrypt offline add magnet:?xt=urn:btih:... --parse-to /quark/downloads
  qrypt offline fetch ./file.torrent --parse-to /quark/downloads --download-to ./out
  qrypt offline list
  qrypt offline show <task-id>
cmd.offline.retry.long: Retry a failed or canceled offline task, starting a fresh attempt under the same task id.
cmd.offline.retry.short: Retry a failed or canceled offline task
cmd.offline.short: Submit and control provider-side offline downloads
cmd.offline.show.long: Show one offline task by id, including its state and, when available, the provider observation.
cmd.offline.wait.example:
qrypt offline wait offline-1a2b3c4d
  qrypt offline wait offline-1a2b3c4d --timeout 10m --json
cmd.offline.wait.long:
Observe an existing offline task until it reaches a terminal state. An
interrupt stops only the observation; the Core task keeps running.
cmd.offline.wait.short: Observe a task to a terminal state without canceling it
cmd.probe.bench.compare.example: qrypt probe bench compare --base before.json --current after.json
cmd.probe.bench.compare.long: Compare a baseline and a current benchmark report and print the per-metric deltas as JSON.
cmd.probe.bench.crud.long: Run a CRUD benchmark against one mount, measuring create, read, update, and delete latency and throughput.
cmd.probe.bench.example:
qrypt probe bench crud --mount cloud
  qrypt probe bench fs --mount cloud --size 64m
cmd.probe.bench.fs.long: Run a filesystem benchmark through the VFS layer on one mount, measuring write and read throughput at the requested size.
cmd.probe.bench.long:
Run machine-comparable benchmarks against mounted drives, or compare two
saved benchmark reports. Benchmarks may write remote or VFS test data.
cmd.probe.bench.xfer.example: qrypt probe bench xfer --source local --dest cloud
cmd.probe.bench.xfer.long: Run a transfer benchmark from --source to --dest, measuring end-to-end throughput between two mounts.
cmd.probe.example:
qrypt probe test crud --mount cloud
  qrypt probe bench fs --mount cloud --size 64m
cmd.probe.long:
Run active diagnostics and benchmarks that may write remote or VFS test
data. Unlike debug, these commands use the mutable control socket.
cmd.probe.test.auth.long: Run a read-only auth driver test that verifies the mount can authenticate and list its root.
cmd.probe.test.auth.short: Run a read-only auth driver test
cmd.probe.test.batchmove.long: Upload a batch of small files through VFS and move them, verifying batch operation correctness.
cmd.probe.test.batchmove.short: Move a batch of uploaded files through VFS
cmd.probe.test.batchupload.long: Upload a batch of small files through VFS, verifying batch upload correctness.
cmd.probe.test.batchupload.short: Upload a batch of small files through VFS
cmd.probe.test.contract.long: Run the driver behavioral contract suite against the mount.
cmd.probe.test.contract.short: Run the driver behavioral contract suite
cmd.probe.test.crud.long: Run a CRUD driver test that creates, reads, updates, and deletes a remote object.
cmd.probe.test.example:
qrypt probe test auth --mount cloud
  qrypt probe test crud --mount cloud
cmd.probe.test.fs.long: Run a VFS filesystem smoke test on one mount at the requested size.
cmd.probe.test.fs.short: Run a VFS filesystem smoke test
cmd.probe.test.instantupload.long: Run an instant-upload driver test, verifying a known file is saved without re-uploading its bytes.
cmd.probe.test.long:
Run active driver or VFS probe tests against mounted drives. These tests
may write remote test data, so they run against the mutable control socket.
cmd.probe.test.multipart.long: Run a multipart or chunked upload driver test at the requested size.
cmd.probe.test.multipart.short: Run a multipart/chunked upload driver test
cmd.probe.test.read.long: Measure a complete read through a mounted filesystem, exercising cold and warm caches and seek behavior.
cmd.probe.test.read.short: Measure a complete read through a mounted filesystem
cmd.probe.test.resume.long: Run a VFS resumable-upload test that interrupts and then resumes an upload.
cmd.probe.test.xfer.example: qrypt probe test xfer --source local --dest cloud
cmd.probe.test.xfer.long: Run a transfer driver test from --source to --dest.
cmd.receive.cancel.long: Request cancellation of a receive task. Cancellation stops observation; a provider-side copy that already started is left in place.
cmd.receive.example:
qrypt receive inspect https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123
  qrypt receive save https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --to /quark/inbox --mkdir
  qrypt receive fetch https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --download-to ./out --keep-cloud
  qrypt receive list --all
cmd.receive.fetch.example:
qrypt receive fetch https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --download-to ./out
  qrypt receive fetch https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --to /quark/inbox --download-to ./out --keep-cloud
  qrypt receive fetch https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --download-to ~/Downloads --select largest:1 --wait
cmd.receive.fetch.long:
Download share content to --download-to. With --to, qrypt first saves
into your drive and downloads that copy, removing the copy it created unless
--keep-cloud is given. Without --to, it downloads the share directly and leaves
the provider unchanged.

The destination may be a qrypt namespace path, a path inside the mount tree, or
a plain local path.
cmd.receive.fetch.short: Download a share's content, with or without saving it first
cmd.receive.inspect.example:
qrypt receive inspect https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123
  qrypt receive inspect https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --passcode
  qrypt receive inspect https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --dir 1234 --json
cmd.receive.inspect.long:
Open a share link and list one directory. Inspection is read-only: it
creates no task, saves nothing, and persists no session token.

A passcode comes from the link's ?pwd= query, from --passcode CODE, or from one
stdin line when --passcode is given without a value.
cmd.receive.inspect.short: Browse a share link without saving anything
cmd.receive.list.example:
qrypt receive list
  qrypt receive list --all --state failed --limit 50
cmd.receive.list.long:
List receive tasks. Active and failed tasks are shown by default; use
--all to include succeeded and canceled ones, and --state or --mount to narrow
the result.
cmd.receive.list.short: List receive tasks (active and failed by default)
cmd.receive.long:
Inspect a share link, copy its content into your own drive provider-side
(转存), or download it locally. The link's provider is inferred from the link,
so no provider name is ever required.

  qrypt receive inspect https://pan.quark.cn/s/<id>
  qrypt receive save <link> --to /quark/inbox
  qrypt receive fetch <link> --download-to ./out
cmd.receive.retry.long: Retry a failed or canceled receive task from its persisted detail. A completed save is not repeated.
cmd.receive.retry.short: Retry a failed or canceled receive task
cmd.receive.save.example:
qrypt receive save https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --to /quark/inbox
  qrypt receive save https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --mount quark --mkdir --select largest:2
  qrypt receive save https://pan.quark.cn/s/abc123 --to /quark/inbox --passcode --no-wait
cmd.receive.save.long:
Copy share content into your own drive provider-side. The destination
must belong to the link's provider; a cross-provider destination is rejected
because a native save never passes bytes through qrypt.

The command blocks until the save is verified at the destination. --no-wait
returns once the task is admitted.
cmd.receive.save.short: Copy a share's content into your own drive (转存)
cmd.receive.short: Inspect, save, or download content behind a share link
cmd.receive.show.long: Show one receive task by id, including its phase, destinations, and per-entry results.
cmd.receive.wait.example:
qrypt receive wait share-1a2b3c4d
  qrypt receive wait share-1a2b3c4d --timeout 10m --json
cmd.receive.wait.long:
Observe an existing receive task until it reaches a terminal state. An
interrupt stops only the observation; the Core task keeps running.
cmd.receive.wait.short: Observe a receive task without canceling it
cmd.root.example:
qrypt mount --config ./qrypt.toml
  qrypt fs list /cloud/photos
  qrypt fs get /cloud/photos/cat.jpg ./cat.jpg
cmd.root.long:
qrypt exposes configured cloud drives as one local FUSE mount point.

Each drive appears as a directory under the mount point, with optional
rclone-compatible content and filename encryption.

Use a command's --config flag to point to a TOML config file, then mount to
start the filesystem, or use fs list/cat/get/put for one-shot operations.
When --config is omitted, qrypt searches ./qrypt.toml, ~/.qrypt/qrypt.toml,
then the platform config directory: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/qrypt/qrypt.toml
(default: ~/.config/qrypt/qrypt.toml) on Unix, or
%AppData%\qrypt\qrypt.toml on Windows.
cmd.root.short: Mounts encrypted cloud drives as a local filesystem
cmd.schema.example:
qrypt schema
  qrypt schema offline fetch
cmd.schema.long:
Print the command tree — subcommands, arguments, and flags — as JSON.

Scripts, editors, and GUIs can read this instead of parsing the rendered help,
so the machine-readable surface stays stable while help wording changes.
cmd.schema.short: Print a command's help as structured JSON
cmd.share.create.example:
qrypt share create /quark/report.pdf --expires 7d
  qrypt share create /quark/docs/a.bin /quark/docs/b.bin --passcode --name release
  qrypt share create /quark/photos --expires forever --limit-visits 10
cmd.share.create.long:
Publish one link for existing content in a mounted drive. All paths must
belong to the same mount; the mount selects the provider. The link is returned
immediately and printed with its URL and expiry.

A provider that answers asynchronously is polled inside the driver under a
bounded window, so a queued link either finishes or reports share_timeout.
cmd.share.create.short: Publish one link for existing content
cmd.share.example:
qrypt share create /quark/report.pdf --expires 7d
  qrypt share create /quark/docs/a.bin /quark/docs/b.bin --passcode=ab12 --name release
  qrypt share list --mount quark
  qrypt share show abcd1234efgh --show-secrets
  qrypt share update abcd1234efgh --expires 30d --public
  qrypt share remove abcd1234efgh
cmd.share.list.example:
qrypt share list
  qrypt share list --mount quark --all --limit 50
cmd.share.list.long:
List links owned by the acting account. Active links are shown by
default; --all also includes expired ones. Use --mount when several mounts are
configured and you do not want the only-mount shortcut.
cmd.share.long:
Publish provider share links for existing content and manage them
afterwards. The mount that owns the path selects the provider, so no command
needs a provider name or a provider share identifier.

  qrypt share create /quark/report.pdf --expires 7d --passcode
  qrypt share list
  qrypt share show <link-id>
cmd.share.remove.example:
qrypt share remove a1b2c3d4e5f6
  qrypt share remove a1b2c3d4e5f6 b2c3d4e5f6a1
cmd.share.remove.long:
Remove links by their qrypt-visible ids. The provider's management id
is resolved internally; the linked content is not deleted.
cmd.share.short: Publish and manage links to content already in a mounted drive
cmd.share.show.example:
qrypt share show a1b2c3d4e5f6
  qrypt share show a1b2c3d4e5f6 --show-secrets --json
cmd.share.show.long:
Show one link by its qrypt-visible link id. Passcodes are masked unless
--show-secrets is given.
cmd.share.update.example:
qrypt share update a1b2c3d4e5f6 --expires 30d
  qrypt share update a1b2c3d4e5f6 --passcode --name release
  qrypt share update a1b2c3d4e5f6 --public
cmd.share.update.long:
Change a link's policy without touching its content. At least one of
--name, --expires, --passcode, or --public is required.
cmd.share.update.short: Change one link's title, expiry, or passcode
cmd.uninstall.example:
qrypt uninstall
  qrypt uninstall --yes
  qrypt uninstall --purge --yes
cmd.uninstall.long:
Remove the qrypt installation created by the install script. On Linux
and macOS that is the ~/.local/bin/qrypt symlink, the binary under ~/.qrypt/bin,
and the installer's PATH block; on Windows it is
%USERPROFILE%\.qrypt\bin\qrypt.exe and its user-scope PATH entry. Your qrypt data
(configuration, cache, logs, and sessions) is kept unless --purge is given.

The command only removes a symlink that points at the managed binary and only
the PATH configuration the installer added, so files it did not create are left
alone. It is safe to run when nothing is installed.
cmd.upgrade.example:
qrypt upgrade
  qrypt upgrade --check
  qrypt upgrade --to v0.5.0
cmd.upgrade.long:
Fetch the newest qrypt release for this platform, verify it against the
published checksum, and replace the running executable in place. The files are
downloaded to a temporary location and only swapped in after verification, so a
failed download or a mismatched checksum leaves the current binary untouched.

Upgrading a development build (a version such as v0.5.3-10-g9d16c54) is refused
because no release can be compared against it; use --force to override. When the
current binary is not writable, the command does not raise privileges itself: it
prints the command to run instead.
cmd.upgrade.short: Update qrypt to the newest release
cmd.version.long: Show the build version, commit, build time, Go version, and platform, or emit them as JSON with --json.
